title: TRANSdiagnostic Research into Emotional Disorders and Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy of the Adaptive Mind
summary: Previous research indicates that patients with different anxiety(-related) and depressive disorders (emotional disorders) bear a close resemblance regarding the development and maintenance as well as psychotherapeutic changes of their problems. Recent studies in individuals with a range of anxiety(-related) and depressive disorders often investigated the relevance of emotional mechanisms (e.g. the regulation of emotions) and used highly standardized psychotherapeutic treatments. The goal of the TRANSTAM project is to moreover figure out the relevance of more basic factors and mechanisms in how we perceive and interact within the real world. The goal is to investigate how these factors and mechanisms can help to predict how individuals respond to naturalistic cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Patients from two outpatient units of the local universities are asked to take part in a behavioral, psychophysiological and magnetic resonance imaging study and to fill in questionnaires e.g. regarding clinical symptoms several times during the course of their cognitive behavioral treatment. The main research questions are if symptoms across different disorders are associated with the investigated factors and mechanisms and if differences in these factors and mechanisms between individuals predict the response to CBT.
conditions: Reaction to severe stress, and adjustment disorders

interventions.name: Patients with an emotional disorder (diagnoses from the sections F32 - F39 or F4 according to ICD-10, exceptions see exclusion criteria) who receive cognitive-behavioral therapy in the outpatient units of the universities of Giessen and Marburg.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who are at the beginning of a psychotherapy (probatory phase) and have psychological problems in the domain of ​​emotional disorders (anxiety (associated) or depressive disorder; diagnosis from the sections F32 - F39/F4, ICD-10), age ≥ 18 years, indication for outpatient CBT treatment, willingness to participate in the study, minimum therapy duration of 12 sessions or regular end of therapy before 12 therapy sessions

Healthy participants who do not currently meet the diagnostic criteria for a mental disorder.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for all participants:
- Presence of certain diagnoses, namely: diagnoses from section F2 (according to ICD-10; e.g. schizophrenia), acute manic/hypomanic episode (diagnosis from the ranges F30 and F31, ICD-10).
- acute suicidal tendencies 
- Presence of psychotic symptoms (e.g. in the context of a major depressive episode)
- organic mental disorders and neurological diseases (e.g. dementia, epilepsy, stroke, multiple sclerosis)
- Age < 18 years
- Insufficient knowledge of German
- Noncorrectable significant impairments in hearing and vision

Additional exclusion criteria study part 2:
- Cardiovascular or respiratory disease (e.g., condition following myocardial infarction, hypertension or hypertension requiring treatment, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease)
- neurodermatitis on the palms of the hands
- current severe hearing loss
- difficulty breathing during simple physical activities (e.g. walking) 
- Pregnancy 

Additional exclusion criteria study part 3 (MRI): 
standard MRI exclusion criteria

Additional exclusion criteria for healthy control participants:
- Presence of mental disorder
